6º de Primaria · Inglés

Going to and will

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Si dices «el sábado voy a ir al cine» y «creo que mañana lloverá», ¿hablas del futuro de la misma manera?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

No exactamente. «Voy a ir» es un plan que ya has decidido: en inglés, I'm going to go. «Lloverá» es una predicción, lo que crees que pasará: I think it will rain. El inglés tiene dos formas principales para el futuro: going to y will.

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: A letter to my future self

Dear Lucas of 2040,

Hello! It's me, you, when you were eleven. Our teacher says we are going to put these letters in a time capsule, and we are going to open it in thirty years. So, if you are reading this, you are forty-one now. That's old!

Right now I love football and drawing comics. I'm going to be a professional footballer, or maybe an illustrator. I think I'll live in a big city, but I might live by the sea, because I love the beach. I definitely won't eat broccoli. Never!

I hope you still have Max, our dog, but he's eight now, so probably not. Sorry, that's a sad thought.

I wonder: will people drive flying cars? Will we have holidays on the Moon? Will robots do our homework? If they do, I'll be very jealous!

Please don't forget the things that make us happy now: playing in the park, laughing with Grandma and reading in bed with a torch.

I promise I'll try to be a good person. Will you keep my promise?

Love from the past,
Lucas, age 11

1. Two ways to talk about the future

In English we often use be going to for plans and intentions (things we decided before): «I'm going to visit my grandparents this weekend». We use will for predictions, quick decisions and promises: «I think it will be sunny», «I'll help you!».

En castellano: going to se parece a «ir a + infinitivo» («voy a visitar»), y will se parece al futuro («visitaré», «ayudaré»). No es una traducción exacta, pero ayuda mucho a recordarlo.

2. Going to: form

The form is: am / is / are + going to + verb. «I'm going to learn the guitar», «She's going to be a vet», «We're going to play a match on Sunday».

Negative: «I'm not going to watch TV tonight», «He isn't going to come». Question: «Are you going to buy a present?» – «Yes, I am. / No, I'm not». «What are you going to do at the weekend?». En castellano: fíjate en que el verbo to be cambia con la persona, igual que en el presente continuo.

3. Plans and evidence

We use going to for plans: «Next summer we're going to travel to Italy. We've got the tickets!». We also use it for predictions with evidence (cuando vemos una prueba ahora): «Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain», «Be careful! You're going to fall!».

En castellano: si ves algo que te hace estar casi seguro de lo que va a pasar (nubes negras, alguien que tropieza), usa going to.

4. Will: form

The form of will is the same for all persons: will + verb. «I will go», «she will go», «they will go». The short form is 'll: I'll, you'll, she'll, we'll.

Negative: won't (will not): «It won't snow tomorrow». Question: «Will you come to my party?» – «Yes, I will. / No, I won't». Careful: after will the verb has no -s and no to: «she will play», not «she will plays» or «will to play».

Vídeo: Simple future (will): inglés para niños · Inglés para niños con Mr Pea (YouTube) · 763 mil visualizaciones

5. Will for predictions

We use will to say what we think or believe about the future, often with I think, I'm sure, probably, maybe: «I think Spain will win the match», «In 2050 people will probably travel in flying cars», «Maybe robots will do our homework!».

En castellano: son opiniones o adivinanzas, sin una prueba que estemos viendo. «I think…» = «creo que…». «I don't think it will rain» = «no creo que llueva».

6. How sure are you?

When we talk about the future, we are not always 100 % sure. English has different ways to say how sure we are:

  • will definitely / definitely won't: we are almost sure. «It will definitely be sunny in Seville in August.» Note the order: «will definitely», but «definitely won't».
  • will probably / probably won't: we think it is likely. «I'll probably go to the cinema on Saturday.» «She probably won't come.»
  • might + verb: it is possible, but we are not sure (puede que, quizás). «It might rain this afternoon.» «I might be a vet one day.» Negative: «I might not go to the party.»

Like will, might is a modal verb: it is the same for all persons (no -s) and is followed by the verb without to: «He might come», not «He mights come» or «He might to come».

Here is the scale, from sure to impossible: will definitely → will probably → might → probably won't → definitely won't.

Vídeo: Verbos modales: May / Might vs. Will · TeacherWhatIDo - Teacher Diana (YouTube) · 110 mil visualizaciones

7. Will for decisions and promises

We use will when we decide something at the moment of speaking (en el momento): «It's cold in here.» – «I'll close the window». «What would you like?» – «I'll have a sandwich, please».

We also use it for promises and offers (promesas y ofrecimientos): «I'll always be your friend», «Don't worry, I won't tell anyone», «Shall I help you?» – «Thank you!».

8. If it rains, we'll stay at home

The first conditional talks about something that will probably happen in the future if another thing happens first. It has two parts:

  • The if part, with the present simple: «If it rains…»
  • The result, with will + verb: «…we'll stay at home.»

More examples:

  • «If you study, you'll pass the exam.»
  • «If we hurry, we won't miss the bus.»
  • «If I have time, I'll call you.»
  • «What will you do if you win the prize?»

Careful! After if we never use will: «If it will rain» is wrong. En castellano pasa lo mismo: decimos «Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa», no «Si lloverá».

We can change the order of the two parts. If the if part goes first, we put a comma: «If it rains, we'll stay at home.» If it goes second, there is no comma: «We'll stay at home if it rains.»

Vídeo: FIRST CONDITIONAL - INGLÉS PARA NIÑOS CON MR.PEA - ENGLISH FOR KIDS · Inglés para niños con Mr Pea (YouTube) · 574 mil visualizaciones

9. Going to or will?

Compare: «I'm going to study Medicine» (a plan, I decided it before) and «Oh, the phone! I'll answer it» (a decision now). «Look at the sky! It's going to snow» (evidence) and «I think it will snow at Christmas» (opinion).

Time words for the future: tomorrow, tonight, next week, next year, this weekend, in the future, soon, one day. En castellano: la palabra de tiempo no decide la forma; lo que decide es si es un plan, una prueba o una opinión.

10. Shall I…? Will you…?

We can also use will and shall in questions to make offers, suggestions and requests. These are very useful when you are with friends or visiting an English-speaking family:

  • Shall I…? to offer help: «Shall I open the window?» «Shall I carry your bag?» (¿Quieres que…?)
  • Shall we…? to make a suggestion: «Shall we play a game?» «Shall we go to the park?» (¿Vamos a…? ¿Qué tal si…?)
  • Will you…? to ask someone to do something: «Will you help me with this box, please?» «Will you close the door?»
  • I'll… to offer immediately: «The phone's ringing!» – «I'll get it!»

And here are some answers:

  • «Yes, please!» · «No, thanks, I'm fine.» · «Good idea!» · «Of course!» · «Sure!»

Shall is mostly used with I and we, and is more common in British English. In American English, people often say «Should I…?» or «Do you want me to…?».

Remember to be polite: add please when you ask for something and thank you when someone helps you. In English-speaking countries, people say «please» and «thank you» very often, even in small everyday situations, like buying bread or getting off a bus. «Will you pass me the salt, please?» – «Of course. Here you are.» – «Thank you!»

11. Reading: my plans for the future

Read Lucía's text: «Next year I'm going to start secondary school. I'm a bit nervous, but I think it will be fun. I'm going to join the school choir because I love singing. When I grow up, I'm going to be a marine biologist. I'll study dolphins and whales. I'm sure the oceans will need our help, so I won't stop fighting for them. Maybe one day I'll live on a boat!»

12. Let's practise: my future box

Write a «future box» (una caja del futuro) to open at the end of secondary school. Write three plans with going to and three predictions with will: «Next summer I'm going to learn to surf», «I think I'll be taller than my dad».

Then interview a partner: «What are you going to do this weekend?», «Do you think you'll live in another country?». Consejo: pregunta con Are you going to…? para planes y con Will you…? o Do you think you'll…? para predicciones.

13. The weather forecast

A weather forecast is a prediction about the weather, so it uses a lot of will, won't and might. Listen to this forecast for Spain:

«Good evening. Tomorrow will be a cold day in the north. It will rain in Galicia and Asturias, and it might snow in the mountains above 1,000 metres. In the centre, it will be cloudy in the morning, but the sun will come out in the afternoon. In the south, it won't rain: it will be sunny and warm, with temperatures of around 22 degrees. There will be strong winds in the Strait of Gibraltar. The weekend will probably be sunny everywhere. Have a good evening!»

Useful weather words:

  • Nouns: sun, rain, snow, wind, cloud, fog, storm, thunder, lightning.
  • Adjectives: sunny, rainy, snowy, windy, cloudy, foggy, stormy. Notice: we add -y to the noun.
  • Temperatures: hot, warm, cool, cold, freezing; «It's 25 degrees».

Now prepare your own forecast for your town for tomorrow and present it like a TV weather presenter, with a map and symbols!

14. Time capsules

A time capsule is a box or container full of objects and messages that people close and hide so that people in the future can open it and learn about the past.

There are some very famous time capsules:

  • In 1795, in Boston (USA), the revolutionaries Samuel Adams and Paul Revere put a time capsule inside the cornerstone of a government building. It contained coins, newspapers and a silver plate. Experts opened it in 2015, 220 years later!
  • In 1939, a company buried a time capsule in New York with a message for people in the year 6939. Nobody alive today will see it opened!
  • Many schools and towns make time capsules to open after 10, 25 or 50 years.

What will you put in your class time capsule? Some ideas: a letter to your future self, a class photo, a newspaper from today, a drawing, a list of your favourite songs and games, and your predictions about the future. When people open it, they will laugh, they might cry, and they will definitely learn something about us.

Vídeo: First look inside Boston time capsule from 1795 · CBS Mornings (YouTube) · 2,2 millones de visualizaciones

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Complete with going to: «We (paint) ___ my bedroom tomorrow. We've bought the paint.»

  1. Es un plan decidido antes (ya hay pintura).
  2. We + are + going to + paint.

Resultado: We're going to paint my bedroom tomorrow.

Ejemplo 2. Choose: «The phone is ringing!» «I (answer / 'm going to answer) it.»

  1. Decisión en el momento → will.
  2. I'll answer it.

Resultado: I'll answer it.

Ejemplo 3. Make it negative: «It will snow tonight.»

  1. Negativa de will: won't + verbo.

Resultado: It won't snow tonight.

Ejemplo 4. Complete: «If it ___ (be) sunny tomorrow, we ___ (go) to the beach.»

  1. If part: present simple.
  2. Result: will + verb.

Resultado: If it is sunny tomorrow, we will go to the beach.

Ejemplo 5. Say it with might: «Maybe I'll go to the party.»

  1. Might = maybe / puede que.
  2. Might + verb, no to.

Resultado: I might go to the party.

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar el verbo to be: «I going to play» → «I'm going to play».
  • Poner -s o to tras will: «she will plays», «will to go» → «she will play», «will go».
  • Decir «willn't» → «won't».
  • Usar will para un plan ya decidido: «I will visit Rome next week, I have the tickets» → «I'm going to visit».
  • Confundir going to (futuro) con going (ir): «I'm going to the cinema» es «voy al cine».
  • Usar will después de if: «If it will rain» es incorrecto.
  • Escribir «He mights come» o «might to come»: might no lleva -s ni to.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Complete: «She ___ (be) a doctor when she grows up.» (going to)

    Ver solución
    is going to be.

  2. Make it negative: «They are going to play tennis.»

    Ver solución
    They aren't going to play tennis.

  3. Make a question: «You are going to buy a new bike.»

    Ver solución
    Are you going to buy a new bike?

  4. Put in order: probably / I'll / tomorrow / you / see.

    Ver solución
    I'll probably see you tomorrow.

  5. Complete: «It ___ snow. I'm not sure.» (might / will definitely)

    Ver solución
    might.

  6. Complete: «If you ___ (eat) all that cake, you'll feel sick.»

    Ver solución
    eat.

  7. What's the adjective? sun, wind, cloud.

    Ver solución
    sunny, windy, cloudy.

  8. Make an offer with Shall I: the window is closed and it's hot.

    Ver solución
    Shall I open the window?

Nivel medio

  1. Complete with will or won't: «Don't worry, I ___ tell your secret.»

    Ver solución
    won't.

  2. What's the short form of «I will»?

    Ver solución
    I'll.

  3. Choose: «Look! That boy (will fall / is going to fall)!»

    Ver solución
    is going to fall (hay una prueba).

  4. Choose: «I'm thirsty.» «I (will get / am going to get) you some water.»

    Ver solución
    will get (decisión en el momento).

  5. Correct: «I think it will raining tomorrow.»

    Ver solución
    I think it will rain tomorrow.

  6. Correct: «If it will rain, we will stay at home.»

    Ver solución
    If it rains, we will stay at home.

  7. Write three sentences about your future with definitely, probably and might.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  8. Complete the first conditional: «If we miss the bus, …»

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: we'll be late for school.

  9. Make a suggestion with Shall we for a rainy afternoon.

    Ver solución
    Shall we watch a film?

  10. When was the Boston time capsule opened?

    Ver solución
    In 2015.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Translate: «El año que viene voy a aprender a nadar.»

    Ver solución
    Next year I'm going to learn to swim.

  2. Write one plan and one prediction about next summer.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I'm going to go camping. I think it will be very hot.

  3. Write a chain story: «If I get a dog, I'll… If I…, I'll…» (four sentences).

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Write a weather forecast for your region for the weekend (six sentences).

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Explain the difference between «I'll go» and «I might go».

    Ver solución
    I'll go: I'm sure/decided. I might go: it's possible, I'm not sure.

  6. Write a letter to your future self like Lucas.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeOur class time capsule

La clase prepara una cápsula del tiempo en inglés para abrirla al terminar Secundaria.

Pasos

  1. Cada alumno escribe una carta a su yo del futuro con will, going to y might.
  2. Escribid predicciones de la clase con el primer condicional: «If we…, we'll…».
  3. Preparad un parte meteorológico del día y otros objetos que representen el presente.
  4. Cerrad la cápsula en una pequeña ceremonia y decidid dónde guardarla.

Producto final: Una cápsula del tiempo con cartas, predicciones y objetos de la clase.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses will, going to and might correctly.
  • Uses the first conditional without will after if.
  • Makes offers and suggestions.
  • Writes a clear letter with future forms.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • El domingo, contad en inglés los planes de la semana: «On Monday I'm going to…».
  • Jugad a adivinar el futuro de la familia en 2050 con frases con will.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de planes, intenciones, predicciones y promesas; futuro con be going to y will (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Cápsula del tiempo con planes y predicciones para abrir en 4º de ESO.
  • Previsión del tiempo de la semana presentada como en la tele.
  • Juego de rol en una cafetería: I'll have…

Fuentes y revisión

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about plans with going to (planes)
  • Make predictions with will and with going to (predicciones)
  • Use will for quick decisions and promises
  • Make negatives and questions with both forms
  • Say how sure we are about the future with might, probably and definitely
  • Use the first conditional: if + present, will
  • Make offers and suggestions with shall and will
  • Understand weather forecasts and write a letter to the future

Palabras clave

future · be going to · plans · will / 'll · won't · predictions · promises · tomorrow · next week

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
